# After a cherry-pick nothing has reconciled the worktree: the objects moved, the
# revealed files did not. Sealing used to write the pre-pick plaintext back over
# the picked objects. Now seal notices that the plaintext is the decryption of an
# earlier object version - git still has it - and leaves the object alone.

sesam-repo admin base.txt changed.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt t
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec sesam add t --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secrets'

exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/changed.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change s'

exec git checkout master
cp $TMPDIR/changed.txt t
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'master: change t'

exec git cherry-pick topic

# The picked object is CHANGED, our plaintext is still BASE - and status can
# tell that it is the old version, not an edit.
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'CHANGED'
exec cat s
stdout 'BASE'
exec sesam status
stdout 'S s'
stdout '1 stale'

# Sealing skips it and says why; the picked content survives.
exec sesam seal
stderr 'not sealed - the object is newer than the plaintext'
stderr 'sesam:   s'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'CHANGED'

# Reveal takes the picked version, and the next seal has nothing to say.
exec sesam reveal
exec cat s
stdout 'CHANGED'
exec sesam seal
! stderr 'not sealed'
exec sesam status
! stdout 'stale'

# --all is the way to insist on the plaintext, stale or not.
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
exec sesam status
stdout '1 stale'
exec sesam seal --all
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'BASE'

-- base.txt --
line one
BASE
line three
-- changed.txt --
line one
CHANGED
line three
